# Benchmarks

Every number on this page comes from a script in this repository. `npm run bench` writes `docs/benchmarks.json`, `npm run media` writes `docs/media/media.json`, and `npm run docs` renders both into this page and the README. Nothing is typed in by hand. When a target is missed, the table says so.

Measured 2026-10-18 at commit `02665d5` on 4 cores of Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.10GHz, Node v22.22.0. Checkpoint `public/checkpoints/pretrained.json` (sha256 `76f89527864e`, 256→128 hidden).

## Against the project goals

| Env steps/s, 4 workers, with inference and resets | ≥ 10,000 | 4,822 | ❌ misses |

## Coverage

Each episode builds a fresh building from the curriculum generator at the given stage and seed, flies kinematic dynamics with the deterministic (mean) action, and stops at 1000 steps on easy buildings or 2400 on hard ones, after 500 steps without new coverage, or after 16 hard collisions. Coverage is the fraction of reachable voxels the drone has seen. Easy is stage 0 (seeds 101, 202, 303, 404, 505, 606, 707, 808). Hard is stage 3 (seeds 4242, 5150, 6160, 7171, 8282, 9393). The curriculum does not draw these seeds during training. Night is the `night-dark` preset: lights off and no flashlight.

The **browser pilot** is what the live demo flies when you pick **Policy**: observations go through the checkpoint's running normalization, which clips to ±5. **Raw observations** feeds the network unnormalized, the way `tests/unit/shipped.test.ts` does. The two paths do not give the same coverage, so both are listed. The **lidar heuristic** is the scripted pilot the screenshot URLs use. It is a floor for comparison, not a learned policy.

| Pilot | Easy day | Easy night | Night / day | Hard day | Hard night | Night / day |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Shipped policy, browser pilot | 67.6% | 65.8% | 97.3% | 16.0% | 15.2% | 95.1% |
| Shipped policy, raw observations | 73.1% | 70.7% | 96.8% | 19.0% | 17.6% | 92.9% |
| Lidar heuristic (baseline) | 29.7% | 29.7% | 100.0% | 17.0% | 17.8% | 104.6% |

## Simulator throughput

Single-thread numbers are Node on the machine above. The worker rows use `node:worker_threads`, two envs per worker, the same rollout code the browser workers run.

| Measurement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Kinematic env step (1 thread) | 0.146 ms · 6,852 steps/s |
| Quadrotor env step, 400 Hz physics (1 thread) | 0.242 ms · 4,133 steps/s |
| Policy inference, SIMD gemm, batch 8 | 0.057 ms per env |
| 4 workers, physics + sensors (lidar heuristic pilot) | 19,268 env steps/s |
| 4 workers, rollout loop with policy-sized network and building rebuild on reset | 4,822 env steps/s |

## Rendering

Recorded 2026-10-18 in headless Chromium (ANGLE (Google, Vulkan 1.3.0 (SwiftShader Device (Subzero) (0x0000C0DE)), SwiftShader driver)). Software rendering is far slower than a laptop GPU, so these are a floor, not a claim.

| Clip | Page | Quality | Mean fps | Backend |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Live PPO training dashboard | `?seed=11&quality=low` | low | 2.7 | webgl2 |
| FPV night flight, shipped policy, easy building | `?seed=11&stage=0&camera=fpv&tod=22&flash=1&lights=0&pilot=policy&quality=low` | low | 3.3 | webgl2 |

## Missions

_Not measured yet. The end-to-end mission runner writes `docs/missions.json`; this table fills in from it._

## Reproduce

```bash
npm ci
npm run bench   # coverage and throughput, about 30 s on 4 cores
npm run media   # headless video capture and frame rates (needs ffmpeg)
npm run docs    # re-render this page and the README tables
```

Seeds can be overridden with `BENCH_EASY_SEEDS=1,2,3` and `BENCH_HARD_SEEDS=...`, and the checkpoint with `BENCH_CHECKPOINT=path.json`.
